result.result: I built the Markdown notes app and every requirement works at both 1280px and 375px. The final run passed 39 unit tests and 16 browser tests in real Chrome; type checking, the linter and the production build are clean. Nothing is committed yet. **How it works** - **Layout:** sidebar plus editor, with Markdown source and preview side by side on desktop. On mobile you see the note list first; opening a note shows the editor with the preview below it, and "← Notes" goes back. - **Notes:** "+ New" creates a note and selects its title so you can type a name straight away. You rename a note by editing its title at the top of the editor. Delete opens a confirmation box with Cancel and Delete (Escape or clicking outside also cancels). Pin/Unpin is in the editor header and pinned notes show a 📌. - **Markdown:** I wrote a small renderer (`src/lib/markdown.ts`) instead of adding a library. It turns every `<` and `>` in a note into plain text before adding any tags, so raw HTML shows up as text and cannot run. Links only work for `http`, `https`, `mailto` and relative addresses, so `javascript:` links come out as plain text. - **Checkboxes:** each preview checkbox knows which source line it came from, so clicking it (or its label) flips `[ ]`/`[x]` on exactly that line. Checkbox-looking lines inside code blocks are left alone. - **Saving:** changes save to localStorage 0.4s after you stop typing, and the header shows "Saving…" then "✓ Saved". Anything not yet saved is written when the page is closed or reloaded. - **Theme:** the light/dark choice is remembered. Before you pick one, it follows the system setting, and the page doesn't flash the wrong theme on load. **Bugs found by clicking through and fixed** 1. "Saving…" appeared on page load with no edit, because React runs the save step twice in development. A test now checks it shows "✓ Saved" on load. 2. On mobile, a short note left a big blank gap between the editor and the preview. A test now checks the preview sits directly under the editor. 3. The sidebar excerpts showed raw Markdown such as `# ## **`. They're now plain text. 4. A task box like `[x]` was counted as a word. It no longer is. One cleanup for you: deleting files needed approval here, so a throwaway test I used to find bug 2 is still at `\bench\cc\opus_notes\e2e\tmp\probe.spec.ts`. Please delete that folder. It passes, but plain `npx playwright test` will also run it. **What I tested and how** - **Logic (`npm test`, Vitest, 39 tests):** headings, emphasis, nested and numbered lists, links, code blocks, checkbox lists; that scripts, ``, `

Both changes are in and work at 1280px and 375px.

- **Empty state:** when there are no notes, the list now says "Nothing here yet. Create your first note." Searching with no results still says "No notes match your search."
- **Word count:** it's now in a thin bar along the bottom of the editor area, aligned right, and no longer in the header next to Pin and Delete. On desktop the bar spans both the source and preview columns, so the count sits under the preview's bottom-right corner. If you meant the corner of the source pane only, I can move it there. On mobile the bar stays at the bottom of the screen, and the editor and preview scroll above it.

All files are in `src/App.tsx`, and nothing is committed. The throwaway test from last time is still in `e2e/tmp/` because deleting it needs your approval, so I ran only `e2e/notes.spec.ts`.

**What I checked**
- **Existing tests:** all 39 unit tests pass (`npm test`), and type checking and the linter are clean.
- **Real browser (Chrome, `npx playwright test e2e/notes.spec.ts`):** all 18 tests pass. That's the 16 earlier ones, each at 1280×800 and 375×740, plus a new test run at both sizes:
  - **Empty state:** I deleted the last note and checked the list shows exactly the new text, still there after a reload.
  - **Word count:** I measured that it sits at the bottom right of the editor area and reads "3 words", then "200 words" after a long note. It stays in the same spot and on screen as the note grows, including on mobile.
- **By eye:** I looked at screenshots of the empty list and of a long note at both sizes. The text and the count's position look right, with nothing overlapping or cut off.
